Oh. I see. Apparently, it would do well for you to clone the repo, modify directly the hardcoded binaries. An example of what could work for you. 
git clone https://github.com/opencode-ai/opencode.git
cd opencode

--

grep -r "smallest possible change" .
grep -r "preserve.*existing.*code" .
grep -r "never make big changes" .
grep -r "NEVER commit changes unless" 

--
cat packages/opencode/src/tool/bash.txt
this is where these configs of NEVER commiting unless explicitely asked are reserved inside. change to something like #"Commit when the user asks you to, or when your AGENTS.md instructs you to."

---
then you build the binary and install it, as always. now, your modified opencode removed the pre-built rule that is possibly clashing with your workflow

sudo mv opencode /usr/local/bin/

today I ran into same problem again, but this time was not because of `.config/opencode/opencode.json `
opencode was updated to v1.16.2, which changed the permission schema. The global agent config at `~/.config/opencode/agents/agent.md` still had the old format:


`permission: allow        # ❌ old format`
The new schema expects a granular object instead:


```
permission:
  read: allow
  edit: ask
  bash: allow
```

Sorry about this. The `wks_global` string is a bad string in your db, I'm not exactly sure how it got there, but in a more recent version we implemented stricter validation of this data which is why you're hitting it now.

You can run this in your db to fix:

```
UPDATE session
SET workspace_id = NULL
WHERE workspace_id = 'wks_global';
```

Run `sqlite3` on your db, and you can find the path with `opencode db path`

The `data retention mode 'default'` in the error is an **account/org setting**, not a request parameter. Per the AWS Fable 5 model card ([Data Retention section](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-anthropic-claude-fable-5.html#model-card-anthropic-claude-fable-5-data-retention)) and the [abuse-detection page](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/abuse-detection.html), Fable 5 refuses all traffic until the account opts into sharing retained inputs/outputs with Anthropic.

**Fix (run once per account; requires AWS CLI ≥ 2.35.1):**
```bash
aws bedrock put-account-data-retention --mode provider_data_share --region us-east-1
```
Check current state with `aws bedrock get-account-data-retention` default is `inherit` (→ resolves to `default`), which is what Fable 5 rejects.

Note this is an account-wide privacy change (inputs/outputs retained up to 30 days and shared with Anthropic for abuse detection / possible human review); revert with `--mode inherit`.

After flipping the setting, the exact `converse` call that previously 400'd now succeeds (`stopReason: end_turn`), and Fable 5 works in opencode with no other changes needed.
